verdict.summary: smtp_command_parse_parameters has inconsistent UTF-8 input validation between auth_response=true and auth_response=false code paths. When auth_response is true, nch is never updated from its initialized value of 1, causing p += nch to advance by only 1 byte per iteration regardless of actual character width. This truncates multi-byte UTF-8 validation to first-byte checking only, bypasses the max_size limit check via undercounted byte consumption, and creates an attacker-controlled code-path selection vector. The signed/unsigned conversion (size_t)(p - parser->end) at line 15 is also a contributing bug.

evidence.reason: nch initialized to 1; never updated in auth_response path (line 13), causing subsequent p += nch (line 22) to advance by only 1 byte per iteration regardless of actual UTF-8 character width.
In auth_response branch, ch reads only single byte at p; nch is NOT updated here (unlike non-auth branch at line 15), leaving it at stale value 1 for the p += nch advancement at line 22.
Non-auth branch properly updates nch with actual UTF-8 character length via uni_utf8_get_char_n. This contrast highlights the missing update in the auth_response branch at line 13.

Advances parser position by nch bytes per loop iteration. In auth_response mode, nch remains 1 (never updated), so p advances by 1 byte per character instead of the actual character length. This undercounts total consumed bytes, causing the max_size check at line 23 to potentially pass oversized parameters.

Post-loop size validation uses (uoff_t)(p - parser->cur). In auth_response mode, p undercounts consumed bytes (only +1 per char vs actual width), so this check may not trigger for lines that exceed max_size when measured in full UTF-8 bytes.

assumptions: parser->auth_response flag is set by caller and may be attacker-influencible
uni_utf8_get_char_n behaves as its name suggests (reads n bytes, returns char length)
smtp_char_is_textstr checks printable/US-ASCII/HTAB range per SMTP spec
